title: Magies Artist Production & QA Tool
description: I designed and built an internal React production and QA tool for the Magies character pipeline. Artists packaged all four Magie evolution stages into a single ZIP and drag-and-dropped the archive into the tool for processing. AWS Lambda prepared the assets, S3 stored the uploaded source package, and the resulting Magie became selectable in a browser-based validation environment where every generation, animation, and expression could be reviewed before approval and promotion into the development, staging, and production pipeline.

sections.title: Dedicated Artist Production Tool
paragraphs: I built the tool specifically to turn completed Spine animation packages into reviewable Magies without requiring the artist to manually prepare application-specific files.

The production workflow was designed around how the finished-animation artist actually worked: package the completed character, upload it, wait for processing, then review the result in the same environment the approval team used.

sections.title: Four-Generation Upload Package
paragraphs: Each Magie consisted of four evolution stages that were packaged together for upload.

sections.title: Drag-and-Drop Workflow
paragraphs: The artist zipped all four generation folders together and drag-and-dropped the archive into the upload section.
The upload could be targeted at either the 2048 or 4096 asset path.
After roughly a minute of processing, the new Magie appeared in the selectable testing list.

sections.title: AWS Lambda Processing
paragraphs: AWS Lambda handled the server-side processing needed to turn the artist upload into the format consumed by the testing application.
This kept the artist workflow simple while moving repetitive preparation work into the automated backend pipeline.

sections.title: S3 as the Testing Source of Truth
paragraphs: Uploaded Magie packages were stored in AWS S3 and remained there.
The testing application loaded from that uploaded location, so the artist and reviewers always knew the version visible in the QA tool was the latest package that had been submitted.

sections.title: Full Evolution Validation
paragraphs: The QA application was designed to validate every evolution stage rather than checking only the final adult character.
Reviewers could inspect the Egg, Baby, Teen, and Adult forms before the Magie was approved for application integration.

sections.title: Animation and Expression Testing
paragraphs: The tool exposed the complete set of animations and expressions for each generation.
The test page acted as the main character QA surface and made it possible to catch animation, expression, asset, or packaging problems before the Magie entered the student programs.

sections.title: Cave Store Evolution Testing
paragraphs: Individual generations could also be loaded one at a time into the Cave Store environment.
This allowed us to test the evolution sequence in context and verify that the character animation did not visually clip against the cave/store presentation.

sections.title: Primary QA Surface
paragraphs: The generated browser-based test environment was the main QA surface for completed Magies.
It allowed the finished-animation artist, me, and one of the company owners to review the same uploaded build before approval.

sections.title: Manual Approval Gate
paragraphs: A Magie was not automatically promoted simply because the upload processed successfully.
The character was manually reviewed and approved before being placed into the development environment.

sections.title: Development to Production Pipeline
paragraphs: After approval, the Magie was added to the development environment.
From there it followed the broader release path through staging and eventually production.
The artist-production tool therefore acted as an upstream validation gate rather than a direct production publisher.

sections.title: Second-Pass Application QA
paragraphs: Passing the standalone Magie QA tool was not the final validation step.
Once the approved Magie was integrated into the actual Essential Skills programs, we performed another pass to confirm that it behaved correctly in the full student experience.

sections.title: Shared Review Workflow
paragraphs: The primary reviewers were the finished-animation artist, me, and one of the company owners.
Using the same browser-based QA environment kept the discussion centered on one known uploaded version rather than separate local copies.

sections.title: Solo Tool Development
paragraphs: I designed and implemented the production tool myself.
The broader Magies character system involved artists and product stakeholders, but the React/Lambda/S3 tooling represented my own development work.

sections.title: Built with the Magies Pipeline
paragraphs: Project files indicate that this tooling began around 2018 as the Magies production pipeline was being established.
The tool should be treated as a dedicated production-support system for the Magies project rather than as a separate unrelated web application.

The legacy card described a React tool that allowed artists to collate project work into the Magie system, upload compressed Spine files, and generate a testing website using AWS Lambda.
This is the same React production tool referenced in the broader Magies Student Reward & Evolution System history.
The dedicated card should focus on the artist upload, processing, validation, approval, and release-support workflow rather than repeat the broader reward/evolution-system story.
